text:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up — we have an offer that needs a comp-band exception and an accelerated start date. Candidate: Alex Chen. Competitive counter on table. Jules needs an answer by EOD.
Finn (Recruiter): Candidate asking to start 2 weeks earlier than our usual notice window. Hiring mgr is pushing to match competitor. Wants +8% above band base + prorated sign-on.
Jules (Hiring Manager): Yep — product needs the role asap. Can we approve +8%? This is within our hiring urgency.
Rory (Compensation): Noting request. +8% is outside L4 band cap (which is +5%). Need comp-committee sign-off or VP tie-break. Also need to document precedent. Can we get justification doc?
Maya (People Ops): I'll pull the compsheet. Finn, can you drop rationale: why candidate, market comps, retention risk?
Finn (Recruiter): Sending brief: "Alex has in-market offer $175k + 20k RSU; our band top is $160k. Candidate will withdraw unless we move now." Link to notes: https://ok.example/offer-notes
Ishaan (Finance): Budget check: Q2 hiring budget for Eng is flexible but requires reclass if base > band. +8% pushes cost center. We can cover if ramped from headcount reserve — need CFO nod.
Sam (Legal): Visa check — candidate has H1B pending transfer; start date needs to align with transfer window. If candidate starts earlier, we need signed offer + acknowledgement. Also want to confirm background clearance timeline.
Rory (Compensation): Quick proposal for routing: `comp-exception -> comp-committee (async) -> Kira (VP Eng) final decision` If comp-committee can't respond in 6 hours, escalate to Kira.
Maya (People Ops): That routing works. I'll kick off the comp-committee notif and tag Kira for escalation.
Offerbot: @channel Offer queue updated: ticket #O-4921 created for comp exception. https://offers.internal/O-4921
Kira (VP Eng): If comp-committee votes to deny, I'm willing to approve up to +7% but not +8% without a solid retention case. Can we propose +7% + 10k sign-on as a compromise?
Jules (Hiring Manager): +7% + 10k sign-on is acceptable but manager requests candidate start on 2026-04-10. Is that feasible with Visa?
Sam (Legal): Visa transfer earliest work date looks like 2026-04-12 in our notes. So 4/10 might be risky. Recommend 4/13 to be safe unless candidate can start remote earlier.
Finn (Recruiter): Candidate prefers earlier. Will ask if remote start is ok for first week. Also confirming they'd accept +7% +10k sign-on.
Rory (Compensation): Comp-committee voting now: Approve +7% with 10k sign-on for retention risk. Recording precedent: document O-4921.
Maya (People Ops): Got the committee approval. Escalating to Kira for final sign-off per routing.
Kira (VP Eng): Approved +7% base bump + $10k sign-on. Also approve 4/13 start date given visa constraints. Please add note: "approved as retention exception; not precedent-setting beyond documented case."
Maya (People Ops): Noted. Preparing final offer packet. Finn, please confirm candidate accepts and update Offerbot when signed.
Finn (Recruiter): Will confirm today. If candidate accepts, I'll trigger Offerbot to send the official offer and schedule start.
Offerbot: Offer O-4921 status: APPROVED (comp bump +7%, sign-on $10,000, start date 2026-04-13). Offer email queued.
Finn (Recruiter): Candidate verbally accepted. Sending signed offer email now. :party-popper:
Maya (People Ops): Thanks team. I'll attach the documented exception to the payroll ticket and close O-4921. Closing notes: route used = comp-committee -> VP Eng escalation, finance notified, legal cleared visa start.
Jules (Hiring Manager): Huge thanks — makes a big difference for roadmap. :raised_hands:
Ishaan (Finance): Noted on reclassing cost. Will update budget docs.
Sam (Legal): I'll log visa conditions and mark 4/13 as start date constraint.
Maya (People Ops): Closing thread; will add to the exceptions log and share monthly summary.
